Halal Food Ho Chi Minh - Lets have lunch before setting off to Da Lat
Dec 2025 • Family
Prior to my trip here, i spoke to Halal@Saigon restaurant staff via FB messenger and they were very helpful. As my request is to book the place (for 8 pax) as well as requesting for an area to do our jamak prayers since we were heading towards Da Lat. They are accomodating to allow us to do our prayers there. Next is the ambience - i think it is pretty alright . The only minus is to go to the toilet , we have to go up the narrow stairs (perhaps if they can see if they can buid a small toilet at level 1 will be much much helpful esp for the elderly and those who have difficulties to climb up. Foodwise, generally they are delicious. The only thing was we asked for additional rice but that time, the rice is still in the midst of "cooking".. Satay gravy need to improve. The rest are fine so far. Beverages also nice. Price wise, i supposed is reasonable. Muslim travellers can have their meal here when they are at Ho chi Minh. 

Food that we ordered but did not manage to take pics as were hungry : Rice, Chicken curry, Omeletter, Tom Yum, Kang Kong Belacan, deep fried squid, sea bass, Thai Tea, juices.....

Excellent halal food in Saigon Ho Chi Minh City
Dec 2024 • Family
Opposite the Juma mosque: Halal@Saigon located at 31 Đ. Đông Du, Bến Nghé, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Vietnam
Great tasting Vietnamese and Malaysian food
Very reasonable
No alcohol served, lots lovely juices, mixes and lassis on the menu.
Good service.

The best halaal halal food options in Ho Chi Minh / Saigon are:
There are a good few halaal halal food options in D.Nguyen An Ninh Street – right next to the Ben Thanh Market. There is a very good money exchange on the corner of the street facing the market– good rates.
Juma salaat in Ho Chi Minh / Saigon is at 12pm.

Could be better
Mar 2023
Atmosphere and place was nice and comfortable. However the waiting time was longer than expected. Close to half an hour to be precise. Food tasted alright, nothing too fancy. The tables next to us was vacant, however it took them a long time to clear the used plates and left over food. So we were sitting beside a table full of stacked plates and leftover foods from previous customers through out the whole time we were having lunch. And that wasn't even at their busiest period. Overall it was average, but service and time for meals to be prepped could be greatly improved.

Very disappointing and not worth the money
Jul 2022 • Solo
Today I decided to go to Halal Saigon for dinner and was so disappointed with the food and drink. I ordered a plate of so called’Jumbo Nasi Lemak with Chicken Curry’ and Teh Tarik. There’s nothing Jumbo about the Nasi Lemak, just a ordinary plate of Nasi Lemak with Coconut Rice, Sambal Chili, Fried Egg, Fried Anchovies, a Deep Fried Drumstick, pickles or so called Achar and a tiny bowl with a piece of small chicken in curry sauce.

Th rice was not flavourful, Anchovies was hard not crunchy, Chicken Drumstick was over fried. Curry chicken…nothing special. As for the Teh Tarik, tea is not strong, very light. 

Check you bill before you do any payment, luckily the waiting staff asked me to check the bill before I do payment. I notice that they charged me for the wet tissue that I did not use, they took the charge for the wet tissue out after I told them.
